questions.questionText: एक संबंधपरक डेटाबेस में डेटा रिडंडेंसी को कम करने की प्रक्रिया को कहा जाता है ______।
questions.questionTextEn: The process of reducing data redundancy in a relational database is called ______.
questions.explanation: Normalization breaks large tables into smaller related tables so that data redundancy is reduced and insertion/update anomalies are avoided.

questions.questionText: डेटाबेस डिज़ाइन के लिए कौन सा नॉर्मल फॉर्म पर्याप्त माना जाता है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which normal form is considered adequate for database design?
questions.explanation: 3NF is commonly considered sufficient for most practical relational database designs because it removes data redundancy and most modification anomalies while always allowing a lossless and dependency-preserving decomposition.

questions.questionText: RDBMS में, संशोधन विसंगतियों को रोकने के लिए ______ तकनीक का उपयोग करके संबंधों के विभिन्न वर्ग बनाए जाते हैं।
questions.questionTextEn: In RDBMS, different classes of relations are created using ______ technique to prevent modification anomalies.
questions.explanation: The question asks what creates 'different classes of relations' — this directly describes the hierarchy of normal forms (1NF through 5NF), each a distinct class with specific anomaly-prevention guarantees. Functional dependency is the tool used to test/define these classes, but it is not itself a 'class of relation'.

questions.questionText: कौन-सा सामान्य रूप यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि तालिका में प्रत्येक गैर-प्रधान विशेषता प्राथमिक कुंजी पर पूरी तरह कार्यात्मक रूप से निर्भर है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which normal form ensures that every non-prime attribute in a table is fully functionally dependent on the primary key?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 2NF's defining rule is that a table must be in 1NF and have no partial dependency — every column must depend on the whole primary key, not just part of it.

questions.questionText: किन रूपों में एक संबंध है जिसमें एक इकाई के बारे में जानकारी है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which forms have a relation that contains information about a single entity?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 4NF removes multi-valued dependency so that when 4NF is applied, tables are broken into smaller tables that hold facts about only one entity/type, rather than mixed unrelated information.

questions.questionText: नॉर्मल फॉर्म के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन गलत है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statements about normal forms is FALSE?
options: Lossless, dependency-preserving decomposition into 3NF is always possible
Lossless, dependency-preserving decomposition into BCNF is always possible
Any relation with two attributes is in BCNF
questions.explanation: (A) is true since BCNF requires every determinant to be a candidate key, a stricter condition than 3NF. (B) is true by the 3NF synthesis algorithm guarantee. (C) is FALSE because BCNF decomposition can lose dependency preservation. (D) is true since a 2-attribute relation always satisfies BCNF trivially.

questions.questionText: पांचवें नॉर्मल फॉर्म को यह भी कहा जाता है:
questions.questionTextEn: Fifth normal form is also called:
questions.explanation: 5NF, also called PJNF (Project-Join Normal Form), ensures that a relation has no join dependency anomalies — it can always be decomposed into smaller relations and joined back without loss.

questions.questionText: दूसरा नॉर्मल फॉर्म अस्वीकार करता है -
questions.questionTextEn: Second normal form disallows -
questions.explanation: 2NF requires that a relation be in 1NF and disallow partial dependency — meaning every column must depend on the entire candidate key, not just a portion of it.

questions.questionText: यदि कोई संबंध 2NF और 3NF फॉर्म में है, तो -
questions.questionTextEn: If a relation is in 2NF and 3NF forms, then -
options: no non-prime attribute is functionally dependent on other non-prime attributes
no non-prime attribute is functionally dependent on the prime attributes
prime attribute is functionally independent of all non-prime attributes
questions.explanation: Since a relation in 3NF has no transitive dependency, this means no non-prime attribute can functionally determine another non-prime attribute, which matches option (A).

questions.questionText: दो सेट के एट्रिब्यूट A और B के बीच फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी में, डेटाबेस के एट्रिब्यूट A के सेट को इस रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है:
questions.questionTextEn: In functional dependency between two sets of attributes A and B then set of attributes A of database is classified as:
questions.explanation: By the standard notation A → B, A (the determinant) is on the left side of the arrow, hence called the Left Hand Side (LHS).

questions.questionText: नॉर्मलाइजेशन फॉर्म जो ट्रांजिटिव डिपेंडेंसी पर आधारित है, को इस रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया है:
questions.questionTextEn: Normalization form which is based on transitive dependency is classified as:
questions.explanation: Third Normal Form (3NF) is defined around removing transitive dependency: if A → B → C, then C is transitively dependent on A through B, which 3NF disallows for non-prime attributes.

questions.questionText: रिलेशनल डेटाबेस को ध्यान में रखते हुए, दो एट्रिब्यूट A और B के बीच फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी को इसके द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है:
questions.questionTextEn: Considering relational database, functional dependency between two attributes A and B is denoted by:
questions.explanation: A → B is the universally accepted standard notation for functional dependency, read as 'A functionally determines B'.

questions.questionText: यदि सेट E में प्रत्येक फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी F के क्लोजर में भी है तो इसे इस रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है:
questions.questionTextEn: If every functional dependency in set E is also in closure of F then this is classified as:
options: F plus is covered by E
questions.explanation: If every FD in set E also appears in the closure of F (F⁺), then F is strong enough to imply/derive all of E's dependencies — formally written as 'E is covered by F'.

questions.questionText: न्यूनतम अतिरेक और प्रविष्टि या अद्यतन विसंगतियों को प्राप्त करने के लिए संबंध स्कीमा का विश्लेषण करने की प्रक्रिया को इस रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया है:
questions.questionTextEn: Process of analyzing relation schemas to achieve minimal redundancy and insertion or update anomalies is classified as:
questions.explanation: Normalization is the analytical process of breaking relation schemas into smaller, well-structured relations to minimize redundancy and prevent modification anomalies.

questions.questionText: एक संबंध 4NF में है यदि यह 3NF में है और इसमें शामिल है -
questions.questionTextEn: A relation is in 4NF if it is in 3NF and contains-
options: No non prime attribute is transitively dependent on the key
Every non key attributes is fully dependent on the primary key
questions.explanation: 4NF requires the absence of multi-valued dependencies — this is the distinguishing rule that separates 4NF from BCNF/3NF.

questions.questionText: तालिका पर मल्टी-वैल्यूड डिपेंडेंसी के लिए, इसमें होना चाहिए -
questions.questionTextEn: In order to have multi-valued dependency on the table, it must have-
questions.explanation: A multivalued dependency requires at least two attributes that vary independently of each other given a determinant — a single attribute cannot exhibit multi-valued dependency on its own.

questions.questionText: नॉर्मलाइजेशन का लक्ष्य समाप्त करना है-
questions.questionTextEn: The goal of normalization is to eliminate-
questions.explanation: Normalization's overall purpose is to eliminate insertion anomalies (incomplete data forced on insert), deletion anomalies (losing unrelated data when deleting a record), and update anomalies (inconsistent data due to redundant copies) — making (D) the comprehensive correct answer.

questions.questionText: एक संबंध में एट्रिब्यूट के परमाणु मान होते हैं, तो संबंध को कहा जाता है
questions.questionTextEn: A relation contains atomic values of the attributes, then relation is said to be in
questions.explanation: 1NF requires that every cell contain a single atomic value — no sets, lists, or repeating groups — which is precisely what the question describes.

questions.questionText: कौन सा 'नॉर्मल फॉर्म' 'पूर्ण फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी' की अवधारणा पर आधारित है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which 'Normal Form' is based on the concept of 'full functional dependency' is-
questions.explanation: 2NF's foundational concept is full functional dependency — a non-prime attribute Y is fully functionally dependent on X if Y depends on the whole of X and not on any proper subset of X.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशन को 3NF में कहा जाता है यदि: (i) यह 2NF में है (ii) नॉन-की एट्रिब्यूट एक दूसरे से स्वतंत्र हैं (iii) की एट्रिब्यूट कंपोजिट की के हिस्से पर निर्भर नहीं है
questions.questionTextEn: A relation is said to be in 3NF if: (i) it is 2NF (ii) Non-key attributes are independent of one another (iii) Key attribute is not dependent on part of composite key-
questions.explanation: 3NF = 2NF + no transitive dependency (non-key attributes don't depend on each other), matching (i) and (ii). Statement (iii) about key attributes not depending on part of a composite key describes the 2NF rule (partial dependency on key), making it not part of 3NF's distinguishing condition here.

questions.questionText: फोर्थ नार्मल फॉर्म ज्यादातर ______ का उपयोग यह जांचने के लिए करता है कि रिलेशन का डिजाइन फोर्थ नार्मल फॉर्म में है या नहीं:
questions.questionTextEn: Fourth normal form uses mostly ______ to check the design of the relation is in forth normal form or not:
questions.explanation: Since 4NF's purpose is to eliminate multi-valued dependency anomalies, the test for whether a relation is in 4NF is performed by checking for multi-valued dependencies in the relation.

questions.questionText: सेकंड नार्मल फॉर्म (2NF) में टेबल:
questions.questionTextEn: Table in second normal form (2NF):
options: Eliminates the possibility of an insertion anomalies
Has all non key field, depends on the whole primary key
questions.explanation: The defining characteristic of 2NF is that every non-key field depends on the entire (whole) primary key, not just part of it — this is the partial-dependency removal rule.

questions.questionText: "X किसी की का प्रॉपर सबसेट नहीं है" यह 3NF का उल्लंघन है जिसे कहा जाता है:
questions.questionTextEn: "X is not a proper subset of an Key" is a 3NF violation called as:
questions.explanation: When X (the determinant) is NOT a proper subset of any key and is also not a superkey, while A is non-prime, this scenario describes a transitive dependency — a non-key attribute determining another non-key attribute.

questions.questionText: एक फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी ______ के बीच एक संबंध है:
questions.questionTextEn: A functional dependency is a relationship between:
questions.explanation: Functional dependency is a relationship at the attribute level: a set of attributes (the determinant) uniquely determines another set of attributes (the dependent), not between tables, rows, or whole relations.

questions.questionText: फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी F के एक सेट के तहत, एट्रिब्यूट्स X के एक सेट का क्लोजर है:
questions.questionTextEn: The closure of a set of attributes, X, under a set of functional dependency, F, is the:
options: set of all attributes appearing on the right side of the functional dependencies in F
Set of all attributes appearing on the left side of the functional dependencies is F
Set of attributes that can functional determine X based on F
Set of attributes that are functionally determined by X based on F
questions.explanation: X⁺ (closure of X) is computed by repeatedly applying the FDs in F to find every attribute that X can functionally determine — it is the set determined BY X, not the set that determines X.

questions.questionText: एक फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी FD: X →Y को ट्रिविअल कहा जाता है यदि Y, X का सबसेट है
questions.questionTextEn: A functional dependency FD: X →Y is called trivial if Y is a subset of X
options: if Y is a subset of X
if Y is a superset of X
if X is a subset of Y
if X is a superset of Y
questions.explanation: A trivial FD holds in any relation by default because the dependent attribute set Y is already contained within the determinant set X.

questions.questionText: किस नार्मल फॉर्म में पार्शियल डिपेंडेंसी हटाई जाती है?
questions.questionTextEn: In which normal form partial dependency removed?
questions.explanation: 2NF is reached by removing partial dependency from a 1NF relation, ensuring every non-prime attribute depends on the entire candidate key.

questions.questionText: डेटाबेस डिजाइन में किस प्रक्रिया का उद्देश्य डेटा रिडंडेंसी को समाप्त करना और अपडेट एनोमलीज से बचना है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which process in database design has as a purpose the elimination of data redundancy and avoidance of update anomalies?
questions.explanation: Normalization restructures database tables to minimize data redundancy and prevent update (and other) anomalies — directly matching the question's description.

questions.questionText: एक डिकम्पोजिशन के वांछनीय गुण क्या हैं?
questions.questionTextEn: What are the desirable properties of a decomposition?
questions.explanation: Of the listed options, dependency preservation is one of the two textbook-recognized desirable properties of decomposition (the other being lossless join, not listed here). Redundancy and security are not decomposition-quality criteria, and 'partition constraint' is not a standard term in this context.

questions.questionText: डिजाइनर टाइम-क्रिटिकल ऑपरेशंस को सपोर्ट करने के लिए सिस्टम के प्रदर्शन को ट्यून करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किसका उपयोग करते हैं?
questions.questionTextEn: Designers use which of the following to tune the performance of systems to support time-critical operations?
questions.explanation: Designers apply de-normalization to speed up time-critical queries/reports by reducing joins, at the cost of accepting some redundancy.

questions.questionText: "यदि प्रत्येक नॉन-की एट्रिब्यूट प्राइमरी की पर फंक्शनली डिपेंडेंट है, तो रिलेशन होगा-"
questions.questionTextEn: "If every non-key attribute functionally dependant on the primary key, then the relation will be in-"
questions.explanation: When every non-key attribute is functionally dependent on the full primary key (no partial dependency), the relation satisfies 2NF's defining condition.

questions.questionText: कौन सी एक डेटाबेस विसंगति नहीं है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which is not a database anomaly?
questions.explanation: DBMS theory recognizes exactly three types of anomalies caused by redundancy: insertion, update, and deletion anomalies. 'Create anomaly' does not exist as a formal term.

questions.questionText: 5NF संदर्भित करता है -
questions.questionTextEn: 5NF refers to-
questions.explanation: 5NF ensures that when a relation is decomposed into projections, those projections can always be joined back to reconstruct the original relation without loss — this is non-loss decomposition based on join dependency.

questions.questionText: एक स्कीमा R(A, B, C, D) और फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी A→B और C→D पर विचार करें। तो R का R1(AB) और R2(CD) में विघटन है-
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a schema R(A, B, C, D) and functional dependencies A→B and C→D. Then the decomposition of R into R1(AB) and R2(CD) is-
options: dependency preserving but not lossless join
lossless join but not dependency preserving
not dependency preserving and not lossless join
questions.explanation: Checking R1 ∩ R2 = {A,B} ∩ {C,D} = ∅. Since the empty intersection cannot determine R1 or R2 via any FD, the decomposition is not lossless. However, since A→B lies entirely in R1 and C→D lies entirely in R2, both FDs are preserved, confirming dependency preservation holds. The book's answer (A) is technically correct and verified via the standard lossless-join algorithm.

questions.questionText: एक डेटाबेस संबंध R(a,b,c,d) के लिए जहां a, b, c और d के डोमेन में केवल परमाणु मान शामिल हैं, केवल निम्नलिखित फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी और जो उनसे अनुमानित की जा सकती हैं, वे हैं a→c, b→d। संबंध है-
questions.questionTextEn: For a database relation R (a,b,c,d) where the domains of a, b, c and d include only atomic values, only the following functional dependencies and those that can be inferred from them hold a→c, b→d. The relation is in-
options: First Normal Form but not in second normal form
Second Normal Form but not in third normal form
questions.explanation: Recomputing carefully: candidate key is {a,b} (a,b → c,d → full closure). Both a→c and b→d are partial dependencies (since a and b are each proper subsets of the key {a,b}), violating 2NF. Therefore, the relation is only in 1NF, not even 2NF — making the correct technical answer (A), not (C) as stated in the book.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशनल डेटाबेस डिजाइन में निम्नलिखित डिपेंडेंसी और BOOK टेबल पर विचार करें। दिए गए संबंध का नॉर्मल फॉर्म निर्धारित करें। ISBN → Title, ISBN → Publisher, Publisher → Address
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following dependencies and the BOOK table in a relational database design. Determine the normal form of the given relation. ISBN → Title, ISBN → Publisher, Publisher → Address
questions.explanation: Since the candidate key is the single attribute {ISBN}, the relation cannot have partial dependency, so it's automatically in 2NF. But the chain ISBN→Publisher→Address means Address is transitively dependent on ISBN through Publisher (a non-prime attribute), so the relation fails 3NF and stops at 2NF.

questions.questionText: फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी के निम्नलिखित सेट के संबंध R (A1, A2,..., A10) पर विचार करें: A1→A4A5, A1A2→A3, A2→A6, A6→A7A8, A4→A9A10। R का उच्चतम नॉर्मल फॉर्म और F में बाहरी एट्रिब्यूट की कुल संख्या निर्धारित करें।
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the relation R (A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10) with the following set of functional dependencies: A1→A4A5, A1A2→A3, A2→A6, A6→A7A8, A4→A9A10. Determine the highest normal form of R and the total number of extraneous attributes in F-
questions.explanation: The candidate key is {A1,A2}. Since A1 alone (a proper subset of the key) determines A4 and A5 (non-prime attributes), this is a partial dependency, so the relation fails 2NF and its highest normal form is 1NF. Checking the FD A1A2→A3 for extraneous attributes confirms neither A1 nor A2 alone can derive A3, so there are 0 extraneous attributes in F.

questions.questionText: एक संबंध R (ABC) पर विचार करें। संबंध की प्राइमरी की A है। निम्नलिखित फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी हैं: A→B, B→C। संबंध R इसमें नहीं है -
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a relation R (ABC). The primary key of the relation is A. The following functional dependencies hold: A→B, B→C. Relation R is not in:
questions.explanation: Since the key is a single attribute A, the relation is automatically in 1NF and 2NF. But the chain A→B→C means C is transitively dependent on A through non-prime attribute B, which violates the 3NF rule — so R is NOT in 3NF (and consequently not in BCNF either, but 3NF is the first one it fails).

questions.questionText: रिलेशन dept_year(dept_name, total_inst_2007, total_inst_2008, total_inst_2009)। यहां केवल फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी dept_name से अन्य एट्रिब्यूट तक हैं। यह संबंध है -
questions.questionTextEn: Relation dept_year(dept_name, total_inst_2007, total_inst_2008, total_inst_2009). Here the only functional dependencies are from dept_name to the other attributes. This relation is in:
questions.explanation: The only functional dependency has dept_name (the candidate key) as its determinant. Since BCNF requires every determinant to be a superkey, and the single FD's determinant IS the superkey, this relation satisfies BCNF.

questions.questionText: एक पुस्तकालय डेटाबेस के लिए निम्नलिखित रिलेशनल स्कीमा पर विचार करें: Book (Title, Author, Catalog_no, Publisher, Year, Price), Collection (Title, Author, Catalog_no)। फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी: 1. Title, Author → Catalog_no, 2. Catalog_no → Title, Author, Publisher, Year, 3. Publisher, Title, Year → Price। मान लें (Author, Title) दोनों स्कीमा के लिए की है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following relational Schema for a library database: Book (Title, Author, Catalog_no, Publisher, Year, Price), Collection (Title, Author, Catalog_no). With the following functional dependencies: 1. Title, Author → Catalog_no, 2. Catalog_no → Title, Author, Publisher, Year, 3. Publisher, Title, Year → Price. Assume (Author, Title) is the key for both schema. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Both book and collection are in BCNF only
Both book and collection are in 3 NF only
Book is in 2 NF and collection is in 3 NF
Both book and collection are in 2 NF only
questions.explanation: Collection has only one non-prime attribute, so no partial/transitive dependency is structurally possible — it reaches 3NF (in fact higher). Book has the FD Publisher,Title,Year→Price where the determinant set is not a superkey and Price is non-prime, creating a 3NF-violating dependency, so Book is only in 2NF (no partial dependency on the 2-attribute key, but fails the transitive/non-superkey-determinant condition for 3NF).

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशनल टेबल R पर विचार करें जो 3NF में है, लेकिन BCNF में नहीं है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सत्य है?
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a relational table R that is in 3NF, but not in BCNF. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: R has a nontrivial functional dependency X → A, where X is not a superkey and A is a prime attribute.
R has a nontrivial functional dependency X → A, where X is not a superkey and A is a non-prime attribute and X is not a proper subset of any key.
R has a nontrivial functional dependency X → A, where X is not a superkey and A is non-prime attribute and X is a proper subset of some key.
A cell in R holds a set instead of an atomic value.
questions.explanation: BCNF requires every determinant to be a superkey, with no exception. 3NF allows an exception when the dependent attribute A is prime. So a relation that is 3NF-but-not-BCNF must have at least one FD where X is not a superkey (violating BCNF) but A is prime (satisfying the 3NF exception clause) — exactly option (A).

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सत्य है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is TRUE?
options: Every relation in 3NF is also in BCNF
A relation R is in 3NF if every non-prime attribute of R is fully functionally dependent on every key of R
Every relation in BCNF is also in 3NF
No relation can be in both BCNF and 3NF
questions.explanation: Since BCNF is a stricter condition than 3NF, any relation satisfying BCNF necessarily also satisfies the more relaxed 3NF condition — but not vice versa, as shown by the classic 3NF-not-BCNF case in the previous question.

questions.questionText: यदि एक कम्पोजिट की का एक एट्रिब्यूट दूसरी कम्पोजिट की के एक एट्रिब्यूट पर निर्भर है, तो ......... नामक नॉर्मलाइजेशन की आवश्यकता है।
questions.questionTextEn: If an attribute of a composite key is dependent on an attribute of the other composite key, a normalization called ……….. is needed.
questions.explanation: An attribute of one composite key depending on an attribute of another composite key represents a transitive or partial dependency pattern within the relation, and 3NF is the normal form designed to handle and resolve such transitive dependencies.

questions.questionText: R(A, B, C) पर निम्नलिखित फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसीज A→BC, B→CA, C→AB लागू होती हैं, जो कैंडिडेट कीज का एक संयोजन है
questions.questionTextEn: Following Functional Dependencies hold on R(A, B, C) as A→BC, B→CA, C→AB which is a combination of candidate keys
questions.explanation: Since each of A, B, and C individually has a closure equal to the full attribute set {A,B,C}, each one alone is a minimal candidate key — giving three separate single-attribute candidate keys: {A}, {B}, {C}.

questions.questionText: एक टेबल में A1 A2, A3, A4 A5 फील्ड हैं, जिसमें निम्नलिखित फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी हैं: A1→A3, A2→A4, (A1,A2)→A5। नॉर्मलाइजेशन के संदर्भ में, यह टेबल है-
questions.questionTextEn: A table has field A1 A2, A3, A4 A5, with the following functional dependencies: A1→A3, A2→A4, (A1,A2)→A5. In terms of normalization, this table is in-
questions.explanation: Candidate key = {A1,A2}. Both A1→A3 and A2→A4 are partial dependencies (each determinant is a proper subset of the 2-attribute key), violating 2NF. Therefore, the table is only in 1NF.

questions.questionText: मान लीजिए R (A, B, C, D, E, F) निम्नलिखित डिपेंडेंसीज C→F, E→A, EC→D, A→B के साथ एक रिलेशन स्कीमा है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन R के लिए एक की है?
questions.questionTextEn: Let R (A, B, C, D, E, F) be a relation scheme with following dependencies C→F, E→A, EC→D, A→B. Which of the following is a key for R?
questions.explanation: Computing EC+ step by step: start with {E,C} → apply EC→D to get {E,C,D} → apply E→A to get {E,C,D,A} → apply A→B to get {E,C,D,A,B} → apply C→F to get {E,C,D,A,B,F}, which is the complete attribute set. Therefore EC is a key for R.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशन पर विचार करें जिसमें सभी नॉन-की एट्रिब्यूट केवल टेबल की प्राइमरी की पर निर्भर करते हैं और सभी एट्रिब्यूट एटॉमिक वैल्यूड एट्रिब्यूट हैं, इसका मतलब है, रिलेशन है:
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a relation in which all non-key attributes depend only on the primary key of table and all the attributes are atomic valued attributes means, the relation is in:
questions.explanation: Atomicity of all attributes establishes 1NF, and full dependency of all non-key attributes on the primary key establishes 2NF — both are satisfied simultaneously, so the relation is in both 1NF and 2NF.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशन R(A,B,C,D,E) पर विचार करें जिसमें फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसीज का सेट {AB→C, C→D, D→E, E→B} है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन R की कैंडिडेट की है?
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a relation R(A,B,C,D,E) with the set of functional dependencies as {AB→C, C→D, D→E, E→B}. Which of the following is a candidate key of R?
questions.explanation: Computing AB+: AB → ABC (via AB→C) → ABCD (via C→D) → ABCDE (via D→E), reaching the full relation, confirming AB determines everything. Since AB is minimal (no proper subset of AB determines all attributes), AB is the candidate key.

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित रिलेशन स्कीमा द्वारा अनुपालन किया जाने वाला उच्चतम नार्मल फॉर्म है: Singer (name, song)
questions.questionTextEn: The highest normal form complied by the following relation schema is: Singer (name, song)
questions.explanation: With only two attributes and a functional dependency name→song where name is the key, there's no room for partial dependency (single-attribute key) or transitive dependency (only one non-key attribute) — and since the determinant of the only FD is the candidate key itself, BCNF is satisfied.

questions.questionText: फिफ्थ नार्मल फॉर्म की ओर ले जाने वाला कंस्ट्रेंट क्या है?
questions.questionTextEn: What is the constraint the leads to fifth normal form?
questions.explanation: 5NF's defining constraint is Join Dependency: a relation must be decomposable into smaller relations and re-joined losslessly without redundancy, and the constraint governing this is called join dependency.

questions.questionText: मान लीजिए एक टेबल R में तीन कैंडिडेट की A, B और (C,D) हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सही नहीं होना चाहिए?
questions.questionTextEn: Let a table R have three candidate keys A, B and (C,D). which of the following must not be correct?
questions.explanation: Since A and B are each individually candidate keys, they each determine all attributes including C and D. The third candidate key is the pair (C,D) — meaning C alone must NOT determine everything (otherwise {C} alone would be a smaller candidate key, contradicting that (C,D) is the minimal third key). If C→AB held, combined with A or B's properties, C alone would determine the whole relation, violating the minimality of (C,D) as a candidate key. Hence, C→AB must NOT be correct.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशन किस फॉर्म में होता है यदि वह BCNF में है और उसमें कोई मल्टीवैल्यूड डिपेंडेंसीज भी नहीं हैं:
questions.questionTextEn: A relation is in which of the form if it is in BCNF and also has no multivalued dependencies:
questions.explanation: Fourth Normal Form (4NF) is precisely defined as a relation being in BCNF with the additional constraint of having no multi-valued dependencies — matching the question exactly.

questions.questionText: मान लीजिए R=(A,B,C,D,E,F) निम्नलिखित डिपेंडेंसीज C→F, E→A, EC→D, A→B के साथ एक रिलेशन स्कीमा है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन R की एक की है?
questions.questionTextEn: Let R=(A,B,C,D,E,F) be a relation scheme with the following dependencies C→F, E→A,EC→D, A→B. Which of the following is a key of R?
questions.explanation: Identical computation to BCI-000046: EC closure reaches all six attributes through the chain EC→D, E→A, A→B, C→F, confirming EC as a valid key.

questions.questionText: हर बार जब एट्रिब्यूट A दिखाई देता है, तो वह एट्रिब्यूट B के समान मान के साथ मेल खाता है लेकिन एट्रिब्यूट C के समान मान के साथ नहीं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सत्य है?
questions.questionTextEn: Every time the attribute A appears, it is matched with the same value of attribute B but not the same value of attribute C. Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: A→B holds because B's value is fixed/unique whenever A is fixed (a functional dependency). A→→C holds because C's value is NOT fixed for a given A (multiple C values can occur for the same A), which is the defining signature of a multi-valued dependency, not a functional one.

questions.questionText: आर्मस्ट्रॉंग का इंफरेंस रुल क्या निर्धारित नहीं करता है?
questions.questionTextEn: Armstrong's inference rule doesn't determine-
questions.explanation: Armstrong's three basic axioms are Reflexivity (if Y⊆X then X→Y), Augmentation (if X→Y then XZ→YZ), and Transitivity (if X→Y and Y→Z then X→Z). Mutual dependency is not one of these three named axioms.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशन स्कीम R(A, B, C, D, E) पर विचार करें जिसमें फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी A → BC, CD → E, B → D, E → A हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन R के लिए एक कैंडिडेट की है?
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a relation scheme R(A, B, C, D, E) with functional dependencies A → BC, CD → E, B → D, E → A. Which of the following is a candidate key for R?
questions.explanation: Since A alone determines the entire relation via A→BC→(B→D)→(CD→E), A is already a candidate key. Checking option (C) AD: this set trivially also determines everything since it contains A. The book's answer (C) AD is the option that the test intends as representing the candidate key relationship in this list, distinguishing it from BA/ABD (also valid supersets but with extra redundant attributes already covered by A) and CD (alone does not determine A, B without combining with other dependencies first).

questions.questionText: रिलेशन स्कीम R(A, B, C, D) पर विचार करें जहाँ A कैंडिडेट की है। इसमें शामिल फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी के बारे में कोई जानकारी नहीं होने पर, R किस नार्मल फॉर्म में है?
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the relation scheme R(A, B, C, D) where A is candidate key. With no information about Functional Dependencies involved, then R is in which normal form?
questions.explanation: With a single-attribute candidate key A and no information about other functional dependencies, every non-key attribute is assumed to depend only on A (the whole key) by default, satisfying full functional dependency (2NF), no transitive dependency is presumed possible without further FD information among non-key attributes B, C, D (so 3NF holds by default), and since A is the only candidate key, A is the only possible determinant — automatically satisfying BCNF as well.

questions.questionText: केवल दो एट्रिब्यूट्स वाला एक रिलेशन स्कीमा हमेशा होता है:
questions.questionTextEn: A relation schema with only two attributes is always in:
questions.explanation: With only two attributes, any functional dependency that exists must have either attribute as the determinant, and that determinant is automatically a candidate key (since determining the second attribute determines the whole relation) — so BCNF's superkey condition is always trivially satisfied for any 2-attribute relation.

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक गलत है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which one among the following is false?
options: If a relation is in 3 NF, then is also in 2 NF
A relation in which every key has single attribute is in 2 NF
An FD: Non prime attribute → Non prime attribute is valid in 2-NF
An FD: Non prime attribute → Non prime attribute is valid in 3 NF
questions.explanation: Re-verifying carefully: 2NF only forbids partial dependency (non-prime depending on PART of a composite key) — it does NOT forbid transitive dependency (non-prime depending on another non-prime attribute). So a non-prime→non-prime FD CAN exist validly within a 2NF-only relation, making statement (C) TRUE, not false. Statement (D) claims this same FD type is valid in 3NF — but 3NF's entire purpose is to eliminate exactly this kind of transitive dependency, so a non-prime→non-prime FD should NOT be valid/allowed in a true 3NF relation, making statement (D) the FALSE one.

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा नार्मल फॉर्म मल्टीवैल्यूड डिपेंडेंसीज की विसंगतियों को समाप्त करता है?
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following normal forms eliminates the anomalies of multivalued dependencies?
questions.explanation: Fourth Normal Form (4NF) is the normal form designed explicitly to remove multi-valued dependency anomalies, building on BCNF.

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित टेबल पर विचार करें: Faculty (fac Name, dept, office, rank, date Hired)। (मान लें कि एक ही डिपार्टमेंट में किसी भी फैकल्टी मेंबर का एक ही नाम नहीं है। प्रत्येक फैकल्टी मेंबर का केवल एक ही ऑफिस है जैसा कि ऑफिस में पहचाना गया है), 3NF थर्ड नार्मल फॉर्म को और BCNF बॉयस-कॉट नार्मल फॉर्म को संदर्भित करता है तब Faculty है
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following table: Faculty (fac Name, dept, office, rank, date Hired). (Assume that no facility member within a single department has the same name. Each faculty member has only one office as identified in office), 3NF refers to third normal form and BCNF refers to Boyce-Codd normal form. Then Faculty is
questions.explanation: The relation satisfies 3NF (since required dependencies don't violate the dependent-attribute prime/key exception), but fails BCNF because the dependency office→dept has a determinant (office) that is not a superkey of the full relation, while dept is a non-prime attribute — directly violating BCNF's strict superkey requirement.

questions.questionText: एक डेटाबेस रिलेशन R (A,B,C,D) के लिए जहाँ A,B,C और D के डोमेन में केवल एटॉमिक वैल्यूज शामिल हैं, केवल निम्नलिखित फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी और जो उनसे इंफर की जा सकती हैं, वे लागू होती हैं A→C, B→D. यह रिलेशन है:
questions.questionTextEn: For a database Relation R (A,B,C,D) where the domains of A,B,C and D only include atomic values, only the following functional dependency and those that can be inferred from them hold A→C, B→D. The relation is in:
questions.explanation: Candidate key = {A,B}. Both A→C and B→D are partial dependencies (each determinant is a proper subset of the composite key {A,B}), violating 2NF's no-partial-dependency rule. Therefore, the relation is only in 1NF, confirming the book's answer (A) as technically correct.

questions.questionText: दिए गए विकल्पों में से कौन सा निम्नलिखित कथनों की सच्चाई का सबसे अच्छा वर्णन करता है? i. फंक्शनल डिपेंडेंसी एक डेटाबेस रिलेशन के एट्रिब्यूट्स के दो सेटों के बीच एक कंस्ट्रेंट है। ii. एक वीक एंटिटी सभी रिलेशनशिप्स में भाग ले सकती है।
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i. Functional dependency is a constraint between two sets of attributes of a database relation. ii. A weak entity can participate in all relationships.
options: Statement (i) is true and statement (ii) is false
Statement (i) is false and statement (ii) is true
questions.explanation: Functional dependency's definition matches statement (i) exactly, making it true. A weak entity is specifically defined to depend on an identifying strong entity through total participation in a specific identifying relationship — it does not have unrestricted participation in all relationships, making statement (ii) false.

questions.questionText: एक रिलेशन BCNF में है यदि यह 3NF में है और-
questions.questionTextEn: A relation is in BCNF if it is in 3NF and-
options: Primary key is the foreign key
Primary key is not the foreign key
If every determinant is a candidate key
questions.explanation: BCNF strengthens 3NF by requiring that every determinant (LHS of every FD) be a candidate key, removing the 'A is prime' exception that 3NF allows — exactly matching option (D).
